source.title: Taking the intentional stance at 12 months of age

confidence_rationale: Foundational and extensively replicated: 12-month-olds attribute goal-directed agency to a 2-D circle on the basis of efficient action-to-goal structure alone, with no face, body or biological motion. That the attribution is body-independent is exactly what the ARCHITECTURAL reading of the AGENCY candidate predicts and the embodied reading does not. Held at 0.72 because goal/agent attribution maps to 'who is the actor' more directly than to self-vs-other causation and controllability, which are covered by other sources (Verschoor et al. 2010; Rochat & Striano 2002).
failure_signatures: Nine-month-olds do not show the effect: before the agency relation is available, the same trajectory is coded as a motion pattern rather than as a means to a goal -- a boundary that carried trajectory content without the actor/goal relation would reproduce the 9-month, not the 12-month, behaviour.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Twelve-month-olds habituated to a small circle jumping over a barrier to reach a large circle looked longer, once the barrier was removed, at the old jumping path (now inefficient) than at a new direct path, indicating they encoded the action as an efficient means to a goal; 9-month-olds did not discriminate.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-545's AGENCY lesion deletes the actor relation and controllability at a boundary. GOV-CONTRACT-1 asks whether the distinction appears before language and whether it is body-independent. Attribution of agency to an abstract stimulus with no body at 12 months answers both: the relation is early and it is not read off a body.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Attributing agency to OTHERS is the social half of the candidate; the self-caused vs externally caused half rests on action-effect binding (Verschoor et al. 2010) and self/other discrimination in specular images at 4 months (Rochat & Striano 2002), which are not this paper. Looking-time inference, infant sample.
mapping.source_context: Human infants 9 and 12 months, habituation-dishabituation to 2-D animated displays.

confidence_components.notes: Domain 2 (developmental) anchor for AGENCY; the abstract-stimulus design is what makes the transfer risk low.
